item.title: How Rio's Law uses specialized license plate to prevent tragedies
item.description: A bill designed to protect neurodivergent drivers and passengers during police encounters is moving to the Georgia House after passing the Senate by a unanimous vote.Known as "Rio’s Law," the legislation would allow individuals with autism or other developmental disabilities to obtain a voluntary, specialized license plate. item.title: Piedmont Fayette breaks ground on massive 7-story patient tower expansion
item.description: Construction is officially underway on a seven-story patient tower at Piedmont Fayette Hospital, marking the largest capital investment by the Piedmont Healthcare system in years.The 200,000-square-foot addition is part of a massive expansion project that hospital officials say will transform the campus to meet the needs of a rapidly growing community. item.description: South Fulton police are asking for the public’s help to locate a man caught on camera allegedly exposing himself outside a local business.South Fulton Police investigators identified the suspect as Robert Lee Harris. He was last seen wearing a light-colored hoodie and sweatpants at 5370 Campbellton Fairburn Road.According to department officials, Harris was confronting an employee when the incident occurred. item.title: High school cellphone ban advances at State Capitol
item.description: Georgia high schoolers could soon be required to stash their cellphones from the first bell to the last under a new proposal moving through the state Capitol.
